newsitem.title: FRANCE: French prosecutors allow asbestos case to go ahead.
newsitem.headline: French prosecutors allow asbestos case to go ahead.

text.p: A legal complaint blaming a cancer on occupational exposure to asbestos has for the first time been allowed to go to court by French prosecutors, justice sources said on Friday.
They said the complaint filed in June by electrician Jean Dalla Torre, 64, alleged that his cancer was caused by inhaling asbestos fibres during the course of his work.
It will now be up to the courts to decide precisely who is legally to blame for the exposure and determine financial damages, the sources said.

"This is an encouraging first step," said Michel Parigot, vice president of France's National Association for the Defence of Asbestos Victims, which lobbied hard for a ban on asbestos products in France.

Parigot said that several similar complaints were pending and predicted a judicial probe intended to fix responsibility for the individual's exposure to asbestos could end up implicating senior state officials.
The association helped compile evidence for the electrician's complaint.
But prosecutors rejected its plea that it be made a party to the complaint in court.

France announced only two months ago that it was banning virtually all uses of asbestos from January 1, 1997, after a scientific report estimated that 2,000 people would die in France this year from contact with the industrial fibre.
News of the ban came long after action by most other industrialised nations against the substance, which was linked by scientists decades ago to lung cancers and other lethal respiratory ailments.
Asbestos was commonly used as an insulation material in the construction industry until the 1970s.
